source: Ministry of Agriculture, Forestry and Fisheries (MAFF), General Directorate of Agriculture, Department of Agricultural Extension — 'បច្ចេកទេសដាំដំណាំឪឡឹក' (Watermelon Cultivation Techniques), 2017.
text:
After basal fertilizer is applied and the bed is irrigated, farmers commonly cover the planting bed with plastic mulch film (silver/black double-sided plastic sheeting). The mulch is unrolled along the length of the bed with the silver/white side facing up and the black side facing down.

Benefits of plastic mulch: the white/silver upper surface reflects sunlight, which helps the plant grow and reduces certain insect pests; the black underside blocks light reaching the soil, which prevents weeds from germinating and growing under the mulch, helps keep soil moisture in, and helps fruit sitting on the mulch stay clean. Thin, low-quality plastic film is not recommended because it tears easily and cannot properly protect the bed.

Method for laying the plastic: (1) unroll the plastic sheet along the bed with the correct side up and pull it taut; (2) pull the film to cover the whole bed and secure both long edges by piling soil or stones along the edges every 3-4 steps to hold it firmly in place; (3) once secured, use a measuring rope or cord to mark the planting-hole spacing along the plastic; (4) punch planting holes through the plastic at the marked spots using a heated hollow tube (e.g., a piece of bamboo or metal pipe warmed over charcoal), making one evenly sized hole per planting position, so that all planting holes are uniform before transplanting or direct seeding begins.
